thread:
Maya R: IncidentBot just fired a page for autoscaler-queue: capacity exhaustion in us-west-2. Seeing queue growth and 503/429 spikes. PagerDuty page: https://pagerduty.example/PD12345 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Page fired for service 'autoscaler-queue' (severity: high). Trigger: scaledown/backoff mismatch -> queue backlog > 12k.
IncidentBot: alert details: avg_queue_depth=12800, p99_inference_latency=2100ms, error_rate=8%.
Maya R: I'm on it. Quick check: are any recent deploys to serving-runtime?
Alex G: No deploys in last 2 hours. Saw a bunch of spot terminations in the cloud console starting ~6m ago for the GPU pool.
Raj P: Acking PD. I'm investigating nodegroup events and quota.
Raj P: Cloud events show "Insufficient capacity for instance type g5.2xlarge" - autoscaler unable to provision new nodes.
Maya R: Ugh spot shortage. Any capacity in on-demand pool or alternate instance types?
Alex G: We have a small on-demand fallback pool but maxNodes=8 and it's already at 100%.
Leah T: Copy. I'll attempt manual scale of the on-demand pool and trigger fallback to g4dn if possible.
Maya R: Prioritize customer-facing routes: route traffic away from large models to smaller quantized variants and reduce batch sizes.
Raj P: Running commands now to increase on-demand node group to 16: ```aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rwd-on-demand-gpu --desired-capacity 16```
IncidentBot: Note: this will take ~3-6 minutes to provision.
Alex G: Also flipping autoscaler config to allow alternate instance types and relax nodeSelector for model-large: ```kubectl apply -f /tmp/autoscaler-fallback.yaml``` (patching Provisioner tolerations and allowedInstanceTypes).
Maya R: Rolling a quick traffic policy: change route weight for hosted-api/model-large -> hosted-api/model-small = 70/30. Patch via console.
Leah T: Done. console change shows 70/30. Monitoring for error rate.
Maya R: Customer impact summary for now: ~15% of authenticated requests to hosted API see >1.5s latency; 2-3 customers with high throughput report 429s. We're throttling by fallback route.
Raj P: On-demand nodes started provisioning, cloud events show 6 nodes active, 10 still pending. Preemption rate dropped.
Alex G: Also enabling KV cache warmup to reduce cold-start token cost; pushing a config: ```PATCH /config/service cache.prefix_warmup=true```
IncidentBot: PagerDuty: Escalation step -> paging SRE secondary in 5m if not acknowledged.
Maya R: Leah, you're primary for next 30m if this persists. Handing off when on-call rotation changes in 28m.
Leah T: Got it. I'll watch provisioning and prepare a manual overlay if autoscaler doesn't adapt.
Raj P: Good news: queue depth down to ~6.2k, p99 latency -> 900ms, error_rate -> 2.1%. Still above baseline but improving.
Maya R: Keep an eye on instance type mix. If g5 remains unavailable, we'll keep fallback policy and keep traffic shifted.
Alex G: I've opened a support ticket with cloud to request capacity in us-west-2 for g5. Ticket #CS-9987.
Maya R: Post-incident actions: 1) increase on-demand fallback cap 2) add additional instance types to allowed pool 3) add healthcheck that triggers earlier fallback routing 4) update runbook to include spot shortage steps.
Leah T: I'll create a short incident doc and link metrics (Grafana snapshots) and timeline. Assigning follow-ups to infra and runtime.
Raj P: Closing PD alert pending stable metrics. I'm leaving the page unack until we confirm last_message_ts.
PagerDuty: Page acknowledged by Raj P.
IncidentBot: If metrics remain stable for 15m, will auto-resolve.
Maya R: Thanks all. Continuing watch; will update once cloud confirms allocation or we stabilize for 15m.
Leah T: Current plan: keep reduced weight on large models for 60m, verify warm cache hit-rate >85%, then gradually shift back.
Raj P: Last check before I step off: queue=4200, p99=480ms, errors=0.9%. Looks good.
Maya R: Marking as mitigated; will file full postmortem with timeline and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
